summary.text: Bletchingley is a 6,600-yard par 72 parkland course in Surrey, opened in 1993.

setting.text: The course is just off junction 6 of the M25, between Croydon and Crawley.
It plays over undulating ground with panoramic views over the North Downs and Weald.
Mixed mature trees and a stream create several water features.

history.text: National Club Golfer says the course opened in 1993.

trivia.text: National Club Golfer says it is overshadowed by nearby Walton Heath, which hosted the 1981 Ryder Cup.

1.text: The opening par 4 is 429 yards, with a generous fairway that kicks right and a second shot that plays longer than it looks.

2.text: The par 3 2nd is 173 yards to a green surrounded by bunkers, where short is better than long.

3.text: The short par 5 3rd offers a chance to pick up a shot, with a fairway bunker right and out of bounds left.

5.text: National Club Golfer calls the par 4 5th one of the best holes, with a risk-reward tee shot across trees.

7.text: The long par 3 7th looks out over the Surrey hills, with out of bounds long.

9.text: The 9th is 491 yards uphill, with out of bounds left and bunkers on the right.

11.text: The par 5 11th is 533 yards, with water lurking right of the green.

14.text: The 14th is a downhill par 3 with a spectacular view.

17.text: The par 3 17th has tall trees on both flanks, out of bounds left and water right of a small green.

18.text: The 18th is a testing par 4 with a green protected by water.

local.text: The club is on Church Lane, Bletchingley, near Redhill, Surrey.
